snippet.title: Charging Costs: What Does EV Charging Cost in 2026? 💶 #electriccars #goe #evcharging
snippet.description:
How you charge your electric car has a HUGE impact on what you end up paying.
Prices can vary quite a bit – depending on whether you’re charging at home, or on the go, or at a rapid charger.

Charging at home is the cheapest option — almost everywhere in the world. In most markets, you're paying roughly 5 euros per 100 kilometres. Public fast charging can easily be two to three times that, and in markets like the UK, even more.

Compared to petrol or diesel, the difference is also clear: a conventional car costs around 12 to 13 euros per 100 kilometres at today's fuel prices. An EV charged at home costs less than half of that.

Your wallbox is your biggest lever. Add a smart tariff, charge overnight, throw in solar if you have it — and EV ownership is hard to beat. 

So plan your charging in a smart way, and you won't just save money — you'll drive more EFFICIENTLY and more SUSTAINABLY.
